tldr: LLMatDesign is a novel language-based framework that uses LLM agents with self-reflection and computational tools to autonomously discover new materials with user-defined target properties in a zero-shot, small-data regime.
contributions: Introduction of LLMatDesign, an interpretable, LLM-powered autonomous materials design framework that eliminates the need for large training datasets
Demonstration of zero-shot adaptability to new tasks and target properties via prompt modification
Closed-loop design process with self-reflection on past modifications incorporated into iterative decision-making
Systematic evaluation showing effective materials design for band gap and formation energy targets with small data
methods: LLMatDesign uses LLM agents (GPT-4o and Gemini-1.0-pro) to propose one of four modifications—addition, removal, substitution, or exchange—to a starting material's composition and structure. Each proposed modification includes a hypothesis explaining the reasoning. The framework then applies the modification, relaxes the structure using a machine learning force field (MLFF), and predicts properties using a machine learning property predictor (MLPP). If the predicted property does not meet the target within tolerance, the LLM performs self-reflection on the outcome, and a modification history message is fed back into subsequent iterations. Experiments used 10 starting materials from the Materials Project database, with up to 50 modifications per run, repeated 30 times, targeting a band gap of 1.4 eV (±10% tolerance) and minimum formation energy per atom.
results: For band gap design, GPT-4o with history required an average of 10.8 modifications to reach 1.4 eV (target), compared to 13.7 for Gemini-1.0-pro with history and 27.4 for the random baseline. GPT-4o with history achieved an average final band gap of 1.39 eV. For formation energy, GPT-4o variants achieved the lowest average formation energies at -1.97 eV/atom (with history) and -1.99 eV/atom (historyless), with GPT-4o with history reaching the lowest minimum of -2.72 eV/atom. Both LLMs consistently outperformed the random baseline across all tasks. History inclusion improved convergence speed for both models.
limitations: Neither GPT-4o nor Gemini-1.0-pro could improve upon the formation energy of starting materials, likely because these materials were already at or near their lowest energy states
Gemini-1.0-pro occasionally suggested chemically infeasible modifications involving noble gases
Historyless variants exhibited oscillation between the same modifications and lack of diversity in generated materials
Self-reflection was only implemented for GPT-4o, not Gemini-1.0-pro
Property validation used surrogate ML models rather than DFT calculations
